Challenges

Sound familiar?

“Our site is responsive, so mobile is handled — right?”

Responsive layout is the start, not the finish. Indexing parity, mobile speed and tap-target UX decide whether responsive actually ranks.

“Content that ranks on desktop is hidden on mobile.”

Under mobile-first indexing, hidden or truncated mobile content effectively does not exist. The parity audit compares both versions line by line.

“Mobile speed scores are red no matter what we try.”

Lab scores mislead; we measure on real mid-range devices and real networks, then fix what users actually experience.

“Desktop converts, mobile just bounces.”

Usually UX debt: tiny targets, intrusive popups, forms built for mice. The UX fix list is prioritised by impact, not taste.

“Google indexes pages we removed months ago.”

Mobile and desktop crawls disagreeing is a parity symptom. One crawl comparison finds where the versions diverged.

“Our app and our mobile site tell different stories.”

Schema and content parity checks align structured data across versions, so search engines see one consistent business.

“Rankings dropped after a redesign we tested on desktop.”

A classic. The fix backlog starts from the mobile crawl of the new build, and future launches get a mobile-first checklist.

“We can’t see mobile performance separately.”

Device-segment reporting is part of the deliverables — mobile traffic, rankings and revenue on their own lines.

How It Works

Mobile-first indexing changed the rules

Google now judges your site primarily by its mobile version. Content hidden on mobile, slow mobile templates and tap targets from 2012 all quietly cap your rankings — on every device.

We audit the mobile experience the way Googlebot's smartphone crawler sees it: rendering, parity, speed on real devices and networks, and the UX signals that decide whether mobile visitors convert or bounce.

FAQs

FAQs on mobile SEO services

Our site is responsive. Isn't that enough?

Responsive layout is the start — indexing parity, mobile speed and UX determine whether responsive actually ranks.

Do mobile rankings differ from desktop?

Yes, often significantly. We track and optimise for both, with mobile as the primary.

Can you test on real devices?

Yes — key templates are checked on physical mid-range Android and iOS devices.

Does this help our app?

For app visibility specifically, see our ASO service; this service covers the mobile web.

Do we need a separate mobile site or app?

Almost never. A well-built responsive site with parity and speed fixed outperforms separate m-dot builds without the maintenance cost.

How do you test mobile speed?

On real mid-range Android devices over throttled 4G, plus field data from real users — not just lab scores on a flagship phone.
